profiles.description: Jose Crespo was a U.S. Army private first class who did not redeploy to Iraq from Fort Carson on June 13, 2008, because his wife had suffered severe complications after giving birth and required his care. profiles.name: Jared Hood
profiles.description: Jared Hood served as a specialist in the Colorado Army National Guard from 2004 to 2007, including assignments in Kuwait and Germany. After hearing an Iraq veteran speak at the 2006 Warped Tour, he went absent without leave in opposition to the Iraq occupation. By 2007 he led the Denver chapter of Iraq Veterans Against the War and later organized publicly during the 2008 Democratic National Convention. The accessible record does not establish an arrest, court-martial, confinement or the precise character of his separation.
profiles.finding: Denver Westword Coors Field protest report matches age, service and IVAW organizing. Follow up original protest photograph, caption and credit.
profiles.rights: No image ingested. Copyright/permission must be documented.

profiles.name: Terri Johnson
profiles.description: Terri Johnson was recruited into the U.S. Army after being promised college benefits. During basic training at Fort Jackson she learned that the promise did not protect her from an Iraq deployment, deliberately failed her final fitness test and went absent without leave on September 28, 2006. She later described returning through military police and spending four days in separation processing. The available account does not identify that processing as jail or stockade confinement. Johnson subsequently organized against military recruitment with the American Friends Service Committee.
profiles.finding: Revcom May 6 2007 explicitly captions Terri Johnson speaking at Greensboro rally; photographer Matt Blalock. Page open returned internal error; retain original asset retrieval and visual verification lead. DLA official and city manager are unverified namesakes.
profiles.rights: No image ingested. Copyright/permission must be documented.

profiles.name: Kevin Lee
profiles.description: Kevin Lee was a U.S. Army private who served in Iraq in 2006. After going absent without leave, he hid in Florida for several weeks and traveled by bus to Toronto in March 2007 because he opposed the war. He sought refugee status with support from the War Resisters Support Campaign and later remained publicly identified among U.S. resisters living in Canada. The accessible record does not establish an arrest, court-martial, confinement or final military disposition.
profiles.finding: UFC fighter, Canadian veteran Naismith, actor, and Kevin Lee Lloyd are unrelated namesakes; military engineer results lack continuity to Toronto resister.

profiles.name: Jimmy Massey
profiles.description: Jimmy Massey served in the U.S. Marine Corps for twelve years and was a staff sergeant with the 3rd Battalion, 7th Marines during the 2003 invasion of Iraq. After challenging the treatment and killing of civilians, he was evacuated from Iraq and diagnosed with depression and post-traumatic stress disorder. With legal counsel, he obtained an honorable medical discharge on December 31, 2003 and became an outspoken antiwar activist. No arrest, court-martial or confinement is documented.

profiles.name: Gerhard Fischer
profiles.description:
Gerhard Fischer crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during an SOA Watch vigil to close the U.S. Army School of the Americas / WHINSEC. Sentenced to 3 months.

Each year on the November anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: SOA resisters book may contain SOA-10 group image. Norwegian Commons portrait, Waffen-SS, German diplomat and industrial portraits are namesakes or unverified.
profiles.rights: No image ingested. Copyright/permission must be documented.

profiles.name: Justin Samuel
profiles.description:
Justin Samuel was an animal rights activist who, with Peter Young, broke onto mink farms in Iowa, South Dakota, and Wisconsin in 1997 and freed approximately 7,000 mink in what was then the largest single ALF action in U.S. history. Samuel fled the United States after the actions; he was arrested in Belgium in September 1999 and extradited to the U.S. He pleaded guilty in 2000 to two counts under the Animal Enterprise Protection Act and was sentenced to two years in federal prison.

In his plea agreement Samuel cooperated with federal prosecutors and named Peter Young as his co-defendant. Young remained at large for seven years before his 2005 capture; the prosecution that sent Young to two years in federal prison rested heavily on Samuel's testimony. Samuel served his sentence and was released well before Young was even captured. He is included here because he served meaningful federal prison time.
profiles.finding: NIJ report and contemporaneous animal-rights coverage match case. Justin Samuel Teff and Justin Samuel Coppola are unrelated namesakes; no portrait selected.
profiles.rights: No image ingested. Copyright/permission must be documented.

profiles.name: Ian Thompson
profiles.description:
Ian Thompson was a Trident Ploughshares activist. Faslane / Coulport fence-cutting. Sentenced to 12 days pretrial + 7 days for unpaid fine.

Trident Ploughshares is the UK direct-disarmament campaign founded in 1998 to nonviolently dismantle the UK's Trident nuclear weapons system. Trident submarines are based at HMNB Clyde (Faslane) and HMNB Coulport, equipped with Trident D-5 missiles leased from the U.S. Navy and warheads built at AWE Aldermaston with U.S. design assistance - making the system a direct extension of U.S. nuclear posture in the North Atlantic.
profiles.finding: 1998 Finnish antimilitarist newsletter independently lists Trident prisoner Ian Thompson. Canadian military photographer and Geograph author not matched; no portrait verified.
profiles.rights: No image ingested. Copyright/permission must be documented.
